items.rawSummary: U.S. and Israeli military preparations persist alongside deadlocked nuclear negotiations, with both sides exchanging conditions, while Iran faces deepening isolation from disrupted oil exports and a nearly three-month internet blackout.
items.analysis: CNN and The New York Times have reported that U.S. and Israeli military officials are finalizing targets for possible strikes on Iran, with operations that could begin as early as next week and could include special forces deployments to Isfahan and Kharg Island to seize enriched uranium. Those plans follow President Trump's return from China and his warnings that the United States would bomb nuclear facilities or 'go in' if nuclear material is not secured. Over the weekend, Trump posted an AI-generated image on Truth Social of U.S. and Iranian warships with the caption 'It was the calm before the storm,' underscoring that military action remains under active consideration. Amid this, diplomatic efforts remain deadlocked: Iran's semi-official Fars News Agency reported that Washington has rejected Iran's demand for war reparations and insists that enriched uranium be transferred out of the country, while the Wall Street Journal detailed an Iranian counter-offer to dilute part of its stockpile and transfer the rest to a third country. Iranian media also published what it described as Trump's five conditions—including no compensation, surrender of enriched uranium to the U.S., and a ceasefire tied to negotiations—and Iran's counter-demands for a full ceasefire, sanctions relief, and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. Netanyahu stated Israel is prepared for 'every scenario' and will speak with Trump later today. Conflicting assessments of Iran's military posture continue, with U.S. intelligence estimating that Iran retains roughly 70% of its missile stockpile and the majority of its Strait of Hormuz positions, while CENTCOM's commander asserts that Iran's command-and-control is collapsing. The country's isolation has grown: POLITICO reports that China has begun to apply significant economic pressure for a deal, Iran has been unable to export oil by sea for nearly a month, and an internet blackout has entered its 12th week.

items.title: Iranian regime governmental centers (unspecified locations), Iran: Iran's Deputy Parliament Speaker Haji Babaei warned that any attack on Iranian oil would deny global access to the region's oil for a considerable period.
items.description: Iran's Deputy Parliament Speaker Haji Babaei warned that any attack on Iranian oil would deny global access to the region's oil for a considerable period.
items.rawSummary: Amid a deadlocked diplomatic exchange of ceasefire terms, Iranian leadership expands military training and austerity messaging, appoints a China envoy, and threatens severe retaliation and oil supply disruption if attacked.
items.analysis: Iranian state television has expanded defense messaging, broadcasting weapons drills inside mosques alongside earlier public firearms tutorials, while President Pezeshkian urged mosques to promote austerity and lifestyle reforms. This dual militarization-austerity push coincides with the planned reopening of the Tehran Stock Exchange after an 80-day closure, signaling an attempt to normalize parts of the economy. Diplomatic maneuvering remains deadlocked: Fars News detailed U.S. ceasefire demands—including the transfer of 400 kg of uranium, nuclear restrictions, and no compensation—while Iran insists on full sanctions relief, asset release, war compensation, and recognized sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz; Iranian state media later confirmed the formal delivery and rejection of those terms, and Iran publicly countered with its own conditions that the U.S. had already indicated it would not accept on compensation and asset releases. Tehran appointed parliament speaker Ghalibaf as special envoy for China affairs to secure Beijing's support, and Pakistan's interior minister held high-level talks with Iranian officials, including President Pezeshkian, in further diplomatic outreach. Meanwhile, China has not committed to freedom-of-navigation operations, the UAE accelerates a port bypass to reduce Hormuz vulnerability, and Iranian officials escalate threats: General Shekarchi warned of a severe response to any renewed U.S. attack, and deputy parliament speaker Haji Babaei stated that an attack on Iranian oil would deny global access to the region's oil for a considerable period, amplifying the risk of resumed hostilities and energy disruption.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz area (Bandar Abbas vicinity), Iran: Iran is formalizing a toll system under the guise of maritime insurance policies, with fees ostensibly covering insurance against attack, as part of efforts to normalize its control over the strait.
items.description: Iran is formalizing a toll system under the guise of maritime insurance policies, with fees ostensibly covering insurance against attack, as part of efforts to normalize its control over the strait.
items.rawSummary: Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has nearly stopped as Iran formalizes a toll system cast as maritime insurance and the U.S. enforces a naval blockade, raising fears of drug shortages and wider supply disruptions.
items.analysis: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has all but ceased, with fewer than five vessels transiting daily compared to a pre-war average of 130, as Iran asserts territorial sovereignty and enforces a selective transit protocol. Iran announced it will soon unveil a 'professional mechanism' to formalize traffic management and fee collection, now framing the toll as a 'maritime insurance policy' that charges vessels for protection against attack, a design meant to normalize its control. U.S. CENTCOM has interdicted 79 Iran-linked vessels, effectively shutting the strait from both ends. U.S.-China talks produced shared opposition to tolls and militarization, but China has not explicitly rejected Iranian sovereignty claims, and concerns persist over potential Chinese arms sales to Iran. Iran is also expanding alternative overland and rail trade routes through China, Pakistan, and Iraq to circumvent the blockade, though these corridors are unlikely to replace the scale of maritime trade. The disruption is raising fears of drug shortages in Europe and threatening supplies of essential goods reliant on Asia-based supply chains.

items.rawSummary: Tribes in Yemen's al-Jawf governorate mobilize against the Houthis over the arrest of a woman claiming to be Saddam Hussein's daughter.
items.analysis: In al-Jawf province, the historically neutral or pro-Ansarullah al-Yatma tribes are threatening military action against Houthi forces following the detention of a local woman known as 'Mira.' She claims to be a daughter of former Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein, allegedly brought into Yemen in 2003 under a new identity by the Saleh government. The unusual claim and the Houthis' handling of the case have triggered a rare tribal mobilization that could strain internal stability within Houthi-controlled territory and complicate Yemen's already fractured landscape.

items.rawSummary: Lebanon and Israel extended their ceasefire by 45 days on May 15, but Israeli strikes on around 100 Hezbollah positions and retaliatory Hezbollah drone and mortar fire over the weekend underscore persistent hostilities along the border.
items.analysis: Lebanon and Israel extended their ceasefire by 45 days on May 15, yet military activity continued unabated. Over the weekend, the Israeli Army said it struck around 100 Hezbollah sites across southern Lebanon, including surveillance posts, weapons depots, and infrastructure tied to attack planning, with operations reaching into the Tyre area. Hezbollah responded with drone and mortar fire against Israeli forces, though no Israeli casualties were reported. These exchanges followed a week in which a Hezbollah drone wounded three civilians near Rosh Hanikra and Israeli strikes killed more than 20 operatives, according to the IDF, while Hezbollah drone operations damaged an Israeli armored bulldozer near Naqoura and a UNIFIL base. The IDF has expanded counter-drone measures, distributing over 158,000 square meters of anti-explosive-drone netting to its forces and intercepting multiple drones, which it labels ceasefire violations. The extension signals diplomatic efforts to manage the volatile situation, but clashes on the ground remain frequent.
